clue.text: Crowded wards need order to admit me

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it inside, so one piece goes within the other
wards that need putting in order are to be rearranged into a fresh sequence

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Hospital wards are overflowing and need someone to sort them out, starting with letting me in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wards' looks like hospital rooms but is only fodder; 'need order' rearranges it into SWARD before 'to admit' lets ME in near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarmed and crowded are synonyms for a place thronged with people.

clue.text: Thus duplicated, it's mediocre

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: Copying something makes it merely average.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so is an informal term for something middling or mediocre.

clue.text: A mother for one who was motherless

parts.note: taken as written
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: Someone acts as a mother to an orphan.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Adam was made from dust, so he had no mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam, the first man in Genesis, was created directly and had no mother.

clue.text: A spot of intelligence?

parts.note: sounds like a little cleverness, but intelligence here is spy information shrunk to a tiny dot

explanation.surface: A small amount of cleverness.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny photographic dot used by spies to carry secret information.

clue.text: A short release from the army

definitions.text: A short release from the army

parts.words: A short release from the army
parts.note: short suggests brief leave, but it means the abbreviated word for discharge from service

explanation.surface: A soldier gets a brief spell of leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a shortened form of demobilisation, discharge from the armed forces.

clue.text: Spectacles in which bulls appear

parts.note: reads like spectacles such as bullfights, but a rifle's aiming devices are where the target's bull's-eye comes into view

explanation.surface: Bullfights and similar shows are spectacles featuring bulls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacles' suggests glasses or shows; it also hints at the things one sees, while a gun's aiming devices are where the bull's-eye of a target appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles are things worth seeing, and a gun's aiming devices frame the bull's-eye of a target.

clue.text: Pressed on amid dire distress

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits within the other
to distress is to batter, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone carried on even in terrible trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress' rearranges DIRE to IRED; 'amid' puts ON in the middle: IR-ON-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressed clothes have been ironed smooth.

clue.text: Details of special importance — about stars?

definitions.meaning: the most notable parts or features
playfully, lights up high in the sky

explanation.surface: The key points of a report on celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Highlights are standout details, and whimsically the stars are lights on high.

clue.text: Take a turn in the air

definitions.text: Take a turn in the air

parts.words: Take a turn in the air
parts.note: sounds like strolling outdoors, but the turn is a flip heels over head

explanation.surface: Go for a stroll in the fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip one's body heels over head through the air.

clue.text: Cashmere weave? I've no idea!

indicators.note: to weave is to interlace threads, so the letters of the fabric word are worked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Someone asks how cashmere is woven and gets a shrug for an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom used when one has no idea of the answer to a question.

clue.text: It may provide a crash course for the fair driver

definitions.text: It may provide a crash course for the fair driver

parts.words: It may provide a crash course for the fair driver
parts.note: a crash course sounds like quick lessons for a fair-minded motorist, but here it is a course of bumping at a funfair

explanation.surface: Something offers intensive lessons to a fair-skinned or just driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash course' and 'fair' are both double-edged: the fair is a funfair, and crashing into others is the whole point of the ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper car at a funfair gives its driver a course full of collisions.

clue.text: She may be amused, despite her stony looks?

definitions.text: She may be amused, despite her stony looks?

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman with a stern face might actually be enjoying herself.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the Gorgon Medusa's gaze turned onlookers to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gorgon of myth whose look turned people to stone.

clue.text: He cheats, using more than one pack of cards?

definitions.meaning: a deceitful person who says one thing and does another

definitions.text: using more than one pack of cards?
definitions.meaning: read literally, a card dealer who handles two packs at once

explanation.surface: A card sharp is caught cheating by dealing from more than one deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-dealer is a duplicitous cheat, and literally one who deals twice over.

clue.text: Cities laid out in a way that's impractical

indicators.note: out signals the letters are laid out in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Towns planned in a dreamy, unworkable way.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealistic aims are lofty but often unrealistic, so impractical.

clue.text: Island with many debts is undependable

parts.note: Capri is an Italian island
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: An island deep in debt cannot be relied on.
explanation.definitionFit: A capricious person is fickle and unpredictable, so undependable.

clue.text: Put on the rack to extract information?

definitions.text: Put on the rack to extract information?

parts.words: Put on the rack to extract information?
parts.note: torture on the rack stretches a victim, and stretching is also coaxing someone into talking

explanation.surface: A torturer stretches a prisoner on the rack to make them confess.
explanation.walkthrough: The rack stretches its victim lengthwise; the phrase for coaxing a person to talk also means stretching them.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax someone into revealing information is an idiom that literally suggests stretching them.

clue.text: Dulcie's bad in geometry

indicators.note: bad means the letters are in a poor state and need rearranging

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Dulcie is hopeless at geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid, the ancient Greek mathematician, is the great name in geometry.

clue.text: Travel to a place overseas

parts.note: to go is to travel
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a trip abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a state in India, a destination far from Britain.

clue.text: Arose from having the call-up date wrong

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to name is to call

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are set in an incorrect order

explanation.surface: Something came about because someone got the conscription date wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call-up' reads as conscription, but 'up' reverses NAME to EMAN; 'wrong' rearranges DATE to ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Emanated means arose or issued from a source.

clue.text: Piece of music that's inspired

explanation.surface: A tune that came from a moment of creative inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a melody, and also the stuff we breathe in when we inspire.

clue.text: Damaged lamp recast in waste material

indicators.note: something damaged is bent out of shape, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A broken lamp gets melted down and remade from scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap metal is discarded metal, waste material kept for recycling.

clue.text: It's completely in Latin

parts.note: the Latin phrase meaning completely or as a whole

explanation.surface: Something is written entirely in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin tag meaning wholly or altogether.

clue.text: Emphatic about corporal being out of place

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: emphatic means insistent
a corporal is an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: Someone insists forcefully that a corporal is in the wrong place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconsistent does not fit with its surroundings, so it is out of place.

clue.text: Expressions of gratitude and disapproval are forbidden

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks
boo expresses disapproval

explanation.surface: Saying thanks or jeering is not allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is prohibited by custom.

clue.text: The bearing of a president?

parts.note: bearing seems to be deportment, but it is a mechanical sleeve sharing its name with an American president

explanation.surface: A head of state's poise and demeanour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bush is a metal lining serving as a bearing, and the surname of two US presidents.

clue.text: Cooked potato with cold joint

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A fried potato served with a cold cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chip is a strip of fried potato, the British word for a French fry.

clue.text: Assumed to have been very upset

definitions.meaning: took up a role or responsibility
to have got into a state, made a fuss

explanation.surface: It was taken for granted that someone had been deeply distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take on' is British informal for getting agitated or upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Took on means assumed a burden, and in informal British usage, made a great fuss.

clue.text: After a small amount, a lot appears excessive

indicators.note: after says the second phrase follows the first in the answer

parts.note: a bit is a small amount
much means a lot

explanation.surface: A little at first, then a great deal, ends up being too much.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something rather more than is reasonable, so excessive.

clue.text: It's regular trade practice

definitions.meaning: patronage from regular ... of a shop
a habit or usual way of doing things

explanation.surface: Something is a routine of the commercial world.
explanation.definitionFit: Custom means a shop's regular patronage and also a habitual practice.

clue.text: Friendly approach to make up for former roughness

parts.note: old means former
chap is roughness of the skin, as in chapped hands

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make amends for past rudeness by being friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Old chap is an affectionate form of address used when approaching a friend.
